description: I'm a 12th grade student with a deep passion for tech, engineering, and space. I've always wanted to build a project like and hope to someday truly advance space exploration; I'm looking for smart and skilled team members 16-18 yo with real drive and desire to build something worthwhile, and you don't have to be proficient in everything to join, as I believe anyone can play a huge role in the success of this project. I hope to build a team ready to face any challenges we encounter along the way.
summary: WeywotEngine is an algorithmic engine that identifies suitable analog locations on Earth of locations on the Moon and on Mars for specific missions. It uses open-data on over 25 different surface and sub-surface characteristics from Nasa and other space agencies and organizations alongside specific mission requirements to identify candidate analogs.
details:
OVERVIEW
WeywotEngine is a full-stack geophysical decision-support console for planetary scientists, robotics teams, and Artemis/Mars campaign planners. Instead of picking Earth field-test sites from static lists or collapsing multiple planetary landing zones into an unrealistic "average" mission, WeywotEngine screens 17,768 terrestrial grid cells (1.0-degree global land resolution) in real time and qualifies candidate analog sites across five physical domains using real NASA climate, orbital planetary imagery, elevation, geology, and open-geography telemetry.

PROBLEM STATEMENT

  1. Planetary test campaigns often rely on a small handful of familiar desert or volcanic test beds without systematic global screening.
  2. Multi-site or multi-phase campaigns frequently average distinct planetary environments together, producing terrestrial recommendations that fit neither target well.
  3. Evaluating Earth analog fidelity requires simultaneous alignment across geochemistry, surface morphology, thermal/UV regimes, aeolian/atmospheric physics, operational logistics, and seasonal campaign weather windows.

HOW WEYWOTENGINE SOLVES THIS

  1. Two-Stage Global Discovery & Qualification Pipeline:
    • Stage 1 screens all 17,768 Earth grid cells under 350 ms using 5-domain feature parity (Geochemistry, Morphology, Thermal/Radiative, Atmospheric/Aeolian, Operations/Logistics), seasonal ephemeris alignment, astrobiology modes, Layer B/C specialization (Subsurface Voids, ISRU Feedstock/O2 Yield, Astrobiology Preservation), and 420 km Spatial Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) for global continental diversity.
    • Stage 2 performs full 365-day sliding-window campaign optimization with rain-cliff and seasonal drift penalties, +/-15% weight perturbation robustness analysis, quantitative hardware engineering gap calculations (mass, dust, thermal gap, traction, communications), and Top-100/250 live NASA/DEM verification.
    • Every selected Mars or Moon target receives an isolated evaluation dossier and an independent ranked Earth shortlist.
    • When no single terrestrial site covers all mission requirements, a minimax 2-Site Split Optimizer partitions domain weights or planetary targets across complementary Earth sites and computes a Cross-Target Compatibility Matrix (CTCM) with Harmonic Versatility Index and Mean Pairwise Rank Dissonance.
    • Interactive 3D Three.js Quadtree Tile Globes and 2D Leaflet Tactical Maps across Earth, Mars, and the Moon (including a calibrated Lunar South Pole illumination inset).
    • Coordinate-first geophysical province synthesis allows clicking anywhere on Mars or the Moon to inspect orbital illumination, seasonal temperatures, and volcanic/basin/polar regimes, or clicking anywhere on Earth to run a live multi-API probe.
    • Natural-language campaign designer (powered by Google Gemini 2.5 Flash with deterministic scientific fallback) that decomposes multi-phase planetary campaigns into component targets, domain weights, and operational constraints, asking clarifying questions only when targets or physics are ambiguous or contradictory.
    • Guided 3-step wizard (Goal -> Target -> Review Earth Sites) for streamlined workflows alongside a full Expert Engineering Console with continuous sliders, numeric bounds, permit-tier filters, pre-Stage-2 slope limits, and SHA-256 reproducible JSON/CSV dossier exports.

TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Zustand 5, Three.js (custom WebGL quadtree tile globe), Leaflet (Canvas tactical maps), Web Workers.
  • Backend: Node.js + Hono HTTP server proxying NASA Trek planetary WMTS tiles, aggregating live multi-source Earth probes (24-hour file-backed cache with bounded concurrency and atomic writes), photon/Nominatim geocoding, and Gemini mission architecture generation.
  • Testing & Verification: Vitest test suite covering physics equations, robust statistics, Stage-1/2 concordance, coordinate target synthesis, Lunar vacuum domain-4 guards, pre-Stage-2 slope filtering, cross-tile DEM stitching, and HTTP API validation.
  • RESOURCE LIST NOTE: The designated Space Agency Partner & Other Data section allowed only 25 individual links, which was not enough to include all 60 partner and other resources. For completeness, all 77 sources used in this project are listed individually below: 17 NASA resources and 60 Space Agency Partner & Other Data resources. Each entry preserves its original resource name and URL.
